candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests anticipatory injury-prevention education and health-promotion teaching.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Injury-prevention teaching for sports and recreation
candidate.educational_objective: Teach that properly fitted, activity-appropriate helmets reduce the risk of serious head and brain injury during sports and recreation but do not guarantee prevention of concussion.

options.A: A properly fitted, activity-appropriate helmet can reduce the risk of serious head or brain injury, but no helmet can prevent every concussion
options.B: A helmet prevents all concussions as long as it is worn during the activity
options.C: Helmet fit and activity-specific certification do not affect protective value
options.D: Helmets are recommended only for professional athletes, not recreational children or adults

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current CDC TBI-prevention guidance states that helmets lower the chance of traumatic brain injury during sports and recreation. Current CDC HEADS UP guidance states that helmets can help protect children and teens from serious brain or head injury but that there is no concussion-proof helmet. CDC also emphasizes proper fit, maintenance, age appropriateness, activity-specific certification, and consistent correct use. B falsely guarantees concussion prevention. C contradicts current helmet-safety guidance. D incorrectly limits helmet use to professional athletics.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports helmet use to reduce serious head/TBI risk while explicitly rejecting any guarantee that helmets prevent all concussions.
candidate.source_locator: CDC 'Preventing TBI' → Key points/Prevention tips: helmets lower the chance for TBI during sports and recreation and are recommended for bicycling and multiple sports/recreation activities. CDC HEADS UP 'Safety Guidelines: Helmets' → Helmet Safety: there is no concussion-proof helmet; helmets can help protect against serious brain or head injury; helmets should fit properly, be well maintained, age appropriate, appropriately certified, and worn consistently and correctly.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: CDC Preventing TBI updated 2025-09-15; CDC HEADS UP Helmet Safety updated 2025-07-28; current at access 2026-08-18
